chakana.title: Chakana
chakana.kicker: Where the Beanstalk touches the Earth
text: Chakana sits high in the Andes, at the top of the city, and the Beanstalk rises from its middle. Nobody here forgets it for a second. The Root climbs out of Volcán Cayambe, a carbosteel mountain of terminals, shops, hotels and eateries that never empties. Above it, the Plaza del Cielo wraps a glass dome where the tether enters the sky. The air is thin and cold, so the plaza is sealed. Its windows look down over the whole glittering sprawl. Freight pods slide into warehouses cut deep into the rock.

The Space Elevator Authority runs the Root, and its yellow jackets walk every concourse. Weyland pays most of the locals, who load cargo, clean rooms and keep the pods on time. Crime is low but not absent. Merchants sell fake Luna rock to tourists, chip-rippers work the crowds, and every gate scans you to the bone. Eastside is the exception, because its poverty makes a lost visitor easy prey. A crew comes here to meet a shipment, catch a contact off a pod, or slip something past the SEA.

base-de-cayambe.title: Base de Cayambe
base-de-cayambe.kicker: The Beanstalk's rough and rowdy port town
text: Base de Cayambe spreads over the foothills under Chakana and feeds on everyone who passes through. Warehouses, microfactories and freight yards crowd the old hill towns, and mag-lev lines and roads run over all of it. Cheap hotels, bars and stim-dens fill the gaps. Old Ecuadorian streets hide behind flashing ads. Beneath the arterials, the Mercado Baja runs for kilometres in neon half-light. Its stalls sell almost anything, and most of it is illegal. Past the edge of Neo-Broadway, a junkyard of trash dunes stretches for kilometres.

The NAPD barely shows up, so Los Scorpiones keep the peace and take their cut. The 14K pushes in at the margins. Spacers, students, veterans and small makers live here because rent is cheap and nobody checks your ID. Watts-Watson builds its fortress arcology and its new towers in the middle of the mud.

rutherford.title: Rutherford District
rutherford.kicker: The city every screen sells you
text: Rutherford is the New Angeles of the newsfeeds. Kilometre-high arcologies and starscrapers march down the flanks of the Andes in tight ranks. Holoparks, slidewalks and spotless L-squares fill the plaza level for tourists and stars. At its heart lies Broadcast Square, kilometres of pedestrian plaza walled by towers so tall they hide the sun. Nobody misses the sun, because every surface glows with ads, news and shows. The NBN arcology is one giant screen. Across the square, the Stock Exchange squats like a steel beehive.

NBN owns the noise, and a hundred smaller media and tech corps fight for a tower nearby. Camdrones and NAPD patrols make the square the least private spot in the city. Below the plaza, the undercity is as grim as anywhere. Workers live in cheap stacks between the factories that make the goods sold upstairs, and con artists prey on the rich above.

esmeraldas.title: Esmeraldas
esmeraldas.kicker: Second best, and proud of it
text: Esmeraldas fills the north of the city with a numbered grid of 30-storey condo rows, from 1st Street to 327th. Shops line the ground floors, planters sag on the corners, and rooftop gardens grow wherever someone bothers. The giant blue dome of Blue Sun Stadium glows above the towers of the old town. On the coast, cranes work the docks of Puerto Maritimo. The unfinished Malecón pier juts out over the water, and the New Beach strip offers greasy waves and cramped holiday flats. Eat Row serves cheap food late into the night.

Millions of working families live here, and the rich stay away. People know their neighbours and name themselves by their street. Even the gangs police their own blocks. District manager Paulus Chopra wants new stadiums, slum clearance and celebrity residents. Blue Sun, Walton-Berndt and Weyland's builders are happy to help him. The human dockworkers are unionised and fierce, and imported bioroids tend to end up floating in the harbour. A crew finds work at the docks, on race nights, or in the half-dark tower of Arcology E42.

nihongai.title: Nihongai
nihongai.kicker: Jinteki's garden town with sharp teeth
text: Nihongai is rich, calm and very green. Gardens hang from the walls of its arcologies, and microparks sit on every roof. On the coast, the Jinteki campus covers more than two square kilometres of streams, paths and pruned trees behind a vine-covered wall. Its long, low headquarters runs half the length of the campus. In the Tourist Quarter, tile roofs and holo-characters line streets of bathhouses, restaurants and a zoo. Down south on the shore, New Akiba is one hot neon pocket. Its stalls sell street-grade and contraband tech.

Jinteki rules here in all but name, and armed drones guard the sky over its campus. Lawyers, lobbyists and young corporate stars rent the flats. Clones live in identical barracks under the Residential Quarter, the cleanest undercity in the city. The yakuza run the crime, and they run it quietly, by the rules. Every gang pays them or disappears. That quiet hides plenty.

laguna-velasco.title: Laguna Velasco
laguna-velasco.kicker: Clean lawns, quiet power, deep shadows
text: Laguna Velasco is the government district, built around the Velasco Ibarra reservoir. White glass arcologies stand on wide lawns, because empty space is the loudest sign of wealth here. City Hall's silver tower rises from Downtown. The NAPD headquarters sits on its own granite block out in the lake. Streetlights glow a soft sunset orange. Joggers run on raised walkways, and sailboats cut across the inlets. In Lakeside, colonial mansions line more than a hundred kilometres of winding shore. There are opera houses, museums and almost no neon.

Old money, politicians and corporate elites own this place. Stressed civil servants keep it running, and the Tri-Maf takes a slice of every contract. Critics of City Hall tend to vanish. Under the plaza lies one of the worst undercities in New Angeles. Police and prisec sweep it clean of squatters and call it voluntary relocation. The utilities here run the deadliest ice in the city. A crew comes for a political job, a blackmail drop, or a run on the Zaracay Park camp.

manta.title: Manta
manta.kicker: A hundred kilometres of party coast
text: Manta stretches over a hundred kilometres along the Pacific in three bands. The Strip runs along the surf with sculpted hotels, beach clubs and a party that never stops. White Beach glows with artificial sand, and Party Row is a block of moored yachts. Behind it, a wall of office towers holds the biotech and IT firms. Inland, secure warehouses and worker housing run to the edge of Rabotgorod. On the southern point, the pearl-grey Haas Arcology rises a full kilometre, straight out of the surf.

Haas-Bioroid owns the skyline, and its labs and academy fill the upper floors of its tower. Rich expats and tourists rule the Strip. The staff who serve them live in the warehouse district and don't care much about the beach. The plaza sits only a few metres above the ground, so rich and poor mix more freely than elsewhere. Offshore, squatters and salvage divers live in the flooded ruins of the Sunken City. In the warehouses, Little Bollywood shoots films with Tri-Maf and yakuza money.

rabotgorod.title: Rabotgorod
rabotgorod.kicker: The Workers' City, now Robot City
text: Rabotgorod is an endless grid of identical barracks blocks. Russian engineers built it on a Soviet model to house the Beanstalk's builders. Today, the old blocks store clones and bioroids between shifts. Humans knock through walls and string gangplanks, ladders and lifts between the buildings. Burned-out husks and mouldy towers stand everywhere in the hot, wet smog. In the north-west, the grey warehouses of Stalingrad line up in sharp rows. In the south, Green Valley gleams with fake grass for the newly rich.

Mafiya landlords run the android barracks and the local politics, and they trade patsies to keep the police away. Jobless humans wait for the next boom that never comes, and Human First feeds their anger at the androids. Labour riots break out often.

la-costa.title: La Costa
la-costa.kicker: The breadbasket, where food means power
text: La Costa is the greenest and emptiest district in New Angeles. Fields, orchards and wetlands roll from the coast to the Ecuadorian border. Glowing agroplex towers and greenhouses break them up, and small villages sit in between. Canneries and fish pens line the shore, and buoy lights blink far out at sea. Machalilla Park protects wild marsh, forest and coast. Acid rain still falls on the crops. At night, the fields go almost black, and only the agroplexes burn.

Farm workers, landowners, scientists and corporate summer guests share the land. The district controls the city's food, and that gives it real political weight. The agricorps fight for monopolies with sabotage and murder, and their towers have armed guards. Los Scorpiones hide in bunkers in the old rainforest. Weyland pushes its revitalisation project and wants the farmland cleared.

quinde.title: Quinde
quinde.kicker: The factory floor that powers everything
text: Quinde was forest once. Builders razed it almost overnight to make room for the first factories near the Beanstalk. Now a flat coastal plain holds sheds, smokestacks and ranks of fusion plants that burn lunar helium-3 for the whole city. Floodlights blaze on the plants, the freight lines and the building sites. Neon is rare. Between the bright factories, the undercity is dark and packed. Workers live in tenements built from stacked shipping containers, joined by catwalks and laundry lines.

Jinteki grows clones in the Meat Market, and Haas-Bioroid builds bioroids in Golem Grove. Their profits flow out to a wealthy few. Jobless humans fill the labour halls. The dockworkers of Local 509 are strong, and hatred of androids runs hot.

guayaquil.title: Guayaquil
guayaquil.kicker: The old metropolis, rotting and crowded
text: Guayaquil is the old Ecuadorian city, swallowed by New Angeles and left to rot. It is the most crowded district of all. In Antiguo, dead proto-arcologies loom over collapsed roads, barrel fires and pools of sewage. Painted colonial houses still fade on the hill at Las Peñas. Tents and shacks cover the four old bridges over the rivers. Nuevo is brighter. Its towers build up in layers and spread sideways into inhabited sky bridges around the Jack Weyland Arcology. Boats and floating squats crowd the black water between them.

Orgcrime runs Guayaquil. The 14K holds the port and the banks, Los Scorpiones keep their old local ties, and the yakuza work the vice trade in Nuevo. The NAPD enters Antiguo only when it has to, so locals turn to the gangs for protection. The black market sells power, medicine, food and gene-mod seeds. Guerrilla solar farms move from roof to roof. A crew can buy anything here, hide anyone, or start a war by accident.
